## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: getting familiar with your vehicle
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The whole manual carries an old content-currency date (stated in part A), so any rule here may have changed since; the freshness debt in part A covers every fact in this section.
The push-pull right-turn instruction is garbled in the extracted text; it is taught by symmetry with the left-turn steps and the hand-over-hand clock positions on the same page [A04].
The phone page prints an older texting rule with its fine alongside the later Hands Free Tennessee law, which bans holding a device at all; both are taught as the manual states them, the hands-free law is presented as the broader rule, and no penalty is given for the hands-free law because the manual prints none (verify TN-VEH-D-PHONE) [A05].
The school-zone phone rule for drivers aged eighteen or older predates the hands-free law and is taught only as the manual words it [A05].
The rear-end collision claim is the manual's own statement about Tennessee crash reports and is taught as attributed to the manual, not as an independent statistic [A04].

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 44 prints a texting ban with a fine not over fifty dollars plus court costs and, on the same page, the later Hands Free Tennessee law without any penalty; confirm the current penalties and whether the older provision still applies.
